text: Caldwell Ridge Analytics needs a network foundation for a new customer-reporting platform, and they already know it has to exist twice -- a small dev network and a larger prod network. This lesson turns the module ideas from Chapter 4 into one real, reusable network module instead of writing the same VNet and subnets out by hand, twice.

The module takes real inputs instead of hard-coded values: vnet_address_space, the CIDR block for the whole virtual network, and subnet_count, how many subnets to carve out of it. A third variable, subnet_newbits, controls how big each subnet is relative to that parent block. Nothing about Caldwell Ridge's environment name or address range lives inside the module itself -- every caller supplies its own values.

Instead of typing CIDR blocks by hand, the module loops subnet_count times with count and calls Terraform's built-in cidrsubnet() function on each pass, passing the parent address space, subnet_newbits, and the subnet's own index. cidrsubnet() computes a correct, non-overlapping block automatically, so adding a seventh subnet later is a one-line variable change, not six more lines of arithmetic.

A module only earns its keep if it hands back what its caller actually needs. This one outputs vnet_id, a subnet_ids list built with the splat operator from every azurerm_subnet instance count created, and the resource group name -- exactly what a root config needs to wire compute or a load balancer into this network later, without reaching into the module's internals.

The module itself never contains a backend block -- only the configuration that calls it does. Caldwell Ridge's root config in envs/dev declares the azurerm remote backend from Chapter 3, naming a storage account, container, and a state key scoped to this environment, then calls module "network" with dev's own values. Keeping the two separate is what makes the module reusable at all.

Lesson 29 built one reusable module and proved it with a single dev deployment. Lesson 30 reuses that exact module source twice -- once for a small dev network, once for a larger prod network -- driven entirely by two different .tfvars files, the real pattern Chapter 5 introduced for managing environments without duplicating configuration.
